title: RIGHT JOIN
description: Learn how to use the RIGHT JOIN clause to return all rows from the right table and matching rows from the left table.

data.text: The RIGHT JOIN is a clause of the SELECT statement that combines data from two or more tables. The RIGHT JOIN starts selecting data from the right table and matching it with rows from the left table. It returns a result set that includes all rows in the right table, whether or not they have matching rows in the left table.

data.alt: SQL Server RIGHT JOIN - select only rows from the right table
SQL Server RIGHT JOIN - rows from the right table only

data.text: If a row in the right table does not have any matching rows from the left table, the columns of the left table in the result set will have NULL values.

data.title: RIGHT JOIN Syntax
data.content: Return all rows from T2 (right table) and matching rows from T1.
data.code:
SELECT
    select_list
FROM
    T1
RIGHT JOIN T2 ON join_predicate;

data.text: In this syntax, T1 is the left table and T2 is the right table. Note that RIGHT JOIN and RIGHT OUTER JOIN are the same. The OUTER keyword is optional.
Using the sales.order_items (left table) and production.products (right table) tables.

data.title: RIGHT JOIN with Products and Order Items
data.content: Return all products and their associated order items.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    order_id
FROM
    sales.order_items o
    RIGHT JOIN production.products p
        ON o.product_id = p.product_id
ORDER BY
    order_id;

data.text: The query returned all rows from the production.products table (right table) and rows from sales.order_items (left table). If a product does not have any sales, the order_id column will have a NULL value.
To get the products that do not have any sales, add a WHERE clause to filter out products that have sales.

data.title: Find Products with No Sales
data.content: Use WHERE order_id IS NULL to find products without sales.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    order_id
FROM
    sales.order_items o
    RIGHT JOIN production.products p
        ON o.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE
    order_id IS NULL
ORDER BY
    product_name;

data.title: RIGHT JOIN vs LEFT JOIN
data.text: A RIGHT JOIN is functionally a reversed LEFT JOIN. You can achieve the same results by swapping the tables and using LEFT JOIN. Many developers prefer LEFT JOIN for consistency.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: RIGHT JOIN returns all rows from the right table and matching rows from the left table.
If no match is found in the left table, NULL values are returned.
RIGHT JOIN and RIGHT OUTER JOIN are equivalent (OUTER is optional).
Use WHERE IS NULL to find rows in the right table with no match in the left table.
